thread.title: Canadian Wide Moat 7 Dividend Growth Portfolio - BAM, It's Now 11 - Brookfield Asset Management Inc. (NYSE:BAM)

author: Dale Roberts
title: Canadian Wide Moat 7 Dividend Growth Portfolio - BAM, It's Now 11 - Brookfield Asset Management Inc. (NYSE:BAM)
text:
For my personal retirement portfolio, I only hold 7 Canadian dividend payers that appear to have a simple wide moat. Canada is unique in that certain companies in certain sectors have worked their way to an oligopoly situation - protected from competition. They are protected by regulations, the Canadian preference and incredible barriers to entry. While this still does not guarantee business success, I feel and hope that it will allow for continued business health, making for continued generous and growing dividends.
Here's the intro to The Dividend Growth Wide Moat 7 From Canada .
The Wide Moat 7 represents just 3 sectors. That said, it "covers" one of the most influential sectors in Canada, the financials, plus the consumer by way of the telcos and energy by way of pipeline/energy names.
Financials-Consumer-Energy Many will certainly offer that 7 companies is not enough. This exercise explores bring the Wide Moat Portfolio up to 15 names and perhaps beyond. That said, as we move to more holdings, we might have to go a little light on that Wide Moat angle. Just as with Alimentation Couche-Tard ( OTCPK:ANCUF ) we will add companies with a wonderful management, an impressive history of long-term success and a scalable business model.
Once again, the number 1 portfolio objective is the attempt to avoid failure. We are looking for long-term financial and dividend health.
The next addition, Brookfield Asset Management ( BAM ), is a Canadian staple and investment darling, and it currently comes in at number 9 on the TSX 60.
Yes, past performance does not guarantee future success, but oh my! Portfolio 1 is BAM. Portfolio 2 is the TSX 60 represented by iShares XIU on the Toronto Stock Exchange.
Brookfield Asset Management is an international conglomerate operating through 4 business platforms.
Yup, it's a monster with competitive advantages.
Real Estate
At the core of core is the real estate holdings. And as their investor page states, it is one of the largest office properties holdings in the world.
Here's an overview of that cash flow cow:
Brookfield Property Partners ( BPY , TSX: BPY.UN) is a diversified global real estate company that owns, operates and develops one of the largest portfolios of office, retail, multifamily, industrial, hospitality, triple net lease, self-storage, student housing and manufactured housing assets. Its investment objective is to generate attractive long-term returns on equity of 12%-15% based on stable cash flows, asset appreciation and annual distribution growth of 5%-8%.
As you can see, the property partner is available as a standalone. One could layer that in with BAM to create an income boost. You can read more on BPY in this recent post by Rida Morwa: " Our Top Investment Idea for 2019: 8.4% Yield and Huge Upside from Brookfield ."
Renewable Partners
Brookfield Renewable Partners ( BEP ) is a global leader in hydroelectric power production, and that is 76% of the portfolio. It is also a leader in the developing area of wind and solar, distributed generation and storage. Once again, it seeks and expects generous gains with long-term annualized total returns of 12-15%, including annual distribution increases of 5-9%. This is also available as a standalone.
Infrastructure Partners
From their site:
Brookfield Infrastructure Partners L.P. ( BIP ) is one of the largest owners and operators of critical and diverse global infrastructure networks which facilitate the movement and storage of energy, water, freight, passengers and data. The company’s objective is to generate a long-term return of 12 -15% on equity and provide sustainable distributions for unitholders while targeting annual distribution growth of 5-9%.
Incredibly, that division has delivered compound annual returns of 15% from 2008.
Private Equity
Once again, that can be accessed as a standalone by way of Brookfield Business Partners ( BBU ).
This unit in itself seeks wide-moat businesses that can then be expanded and made more profitable due to Brookfield's international and operational expertise.
It partners closely with management teams to enable business success over the long term, targeting both market leaders and businesses poised for growth through operational and other improvements. These are generally businesses with high barriers to entry, low production costs and the potential to benefit from Brookfield’s global expertise as an owner and operator of real assets.
Again, they seek annual, long-term total returns in the areas of 15%. This is a unique opportunity for the mom-and-pop investor, as alternative assets are usually reserved for the rich. That said, for Canadian investors, I recently penned on a Canadian Robo Advisor, WealthBar , that is partnered with a private equity firm.
The Tota l Brookfield Package While the individual business lines are available, I'd suggest The Full Monty for the Canadian Wide Moat Portfolio.
The very popular and most read REIT expert on Seeking Alpha, Brad Thomas, likes Brookfield a lot, to say the least. This from his recent review.
That's more than a strong recommendation. Brad went on to describe that Brookfield is the Berkshire Hathaway of hard assets. For more analysis, you can have a read of Brad's article, " Brookfield Asset Management: You've Seen The Rest, Now Invest In The Best ."
My readers will now that I like to keep things simple. From Morningstar, here are the key stats for a 10-year period. We have an operator that knows how to expand revenues, profits, dividends and cash flow over time. It operates in growth-oriented segments. Once again, the company plans for generous, market-beating returns, and it has been more than successful on that front.
That said, as Brad pointed out in his article (and as you'll observe from those stock charts), BAM can be a very volatile stock.
The yield is quite low at 1.5%, but while the dividend growth history is "lumpy," it is very generous over time. Dividend Growth Investing and Retirement shows the dividend growth history at 6 years.
Given my new life work stage , if I were to add this to my personal portfolio, I'd be in it for the total return prospects. And certainly, if I can work my way back into an income setting where I can be an accumulator, BAM would be at the top of my list. Wish me luck on that.
